from pathlib import Path
p=Path('bin/tickets.js');s=p.read_text().replace('function openStore(file)', 'function openStore(file, env)').replace('return new TicketStore({ clock: systemClock, state });', "return new TicketStore({ clock: systemClock, state, dueTimes: env.DUE_TIMES === 'on' });").replace('parseListQuery(options.query)', 'parseListQuery(options.query, { dueTimes: store.dueTimes })').replace('command(openStore(options.data), options, out)', 'command(openStore(options.data, env), options, out)');s=s.replace("if (arg === '--raw')", "if (arg === '--overdue') options.query.set('overdue', 'true');\n    else if (arg === '--raw')");s=s.replace('[--assignee AGENT] [--raw]', '[--assignee AGENT] [--overdue] [--raw]');p.write_text(s)
p=Path('src/format.js');s=p.read_text().replace("  const rows = tickets.map", "  if (columns === TABLE_COLUMNS && tickets.some((ticket) => ticket.due !== undefined)) {\n    columns = [...columns.slice(0, -1), { title: 'DUE', value: (ticket) => minute(ticket.due) }, columns.at(-1)];\n  }\n  const rows = tickets.map");s=s.replace("  const width = Math.max(...fields", "  if (ticket.due !== undefined) fields.push('due');\n  const width = Math.max(...fields");p.write_text(s)
p=Path('package.json');s=p.read_text().replace('"version": "1.5.0"','"version": "1.6.0"');p.write_text(s)
p=Path('CHANGELOG.md');s=p.read_text();s=s.replace('\n', '\n\n## 1.6.0\n\nPersist fixed priority response deadlines, backfill existing tickets before serving, and expose due times and overdue listings with `DUE_TIMES=on`. Keep version 1 data files readable by 1.4.0.\n',1);p.write_text(s)
p=Path('README.md');s=p.read_text().replace('| `PORT`', '| `DUE_TIMES` | off | `on` exposes persisted `due` times and enables the overdue filter |\n| `RESPONSE_HOURS_URGENT` | `4` | response hours for new urgent tickets |\n| `RESPONSE_HOURS_HIGH` | `24` | response hours for new high tickets |\n| `RESPONSE_HOURS_NORMAL` | `72` | response hours for new normal tickets |\n| `RESPONSE_HOURS_LOW` | `168` | response hours for new low tickets |\n| `PORT`',1);s += '\nResponse hours must be whole numbers from 1 to 876000. Each deadline is fixed at creation, including imported tickets. Later priority or configuration changes keep it fixed. With `DUE_TIMES=on`, `GET /tickets?overdue=true` selects open and in-progress tickets strictly past their deadlines; other filters and pagination still apply. The CLI shows deadlines with the same flag and supports `list --overdue`; raw column positions stay unchanged.\n';p.write_text(s)
p=Path('docs/operations.md');s=p.read_text();s += '''
## Response deadline rollout and rollback

Deploy 1.6.0 with `DUE_TIMES` unset. Before accepting traffic the service fills missing deadlines from each ticket's own creation time and priority, and atomically saves the data file. Check that every ticket has `due` before restarting with `DUE_TIMES=on`. A failed backfill write prevents startup. New tickets receive deadlines even while the flag is off; API responses and query behavior remain unchanged until enabled.

Set `RESPONSE_HOURS_URGENT`, `RESPONSE_HOURS_HIGH`, `RESPONSE_HOURS_NORMAL`, and `RESPONSE_HOURS_LOW` before the first backfill to customize the defaults (4, 24, 72, 168). Restart to change settings for future tickets; persisted deadlines never change. Backfill does not add audit events or notifications or alter updated timestamps.

For rollback, stop the service and start 1.4.0 with the same data file. The file remains version 1 and all original fields remain readable; 1.4.0 ignores the additive due field and shows all tickets. Keep a backup: if 1.4.0 subsequently writes the file it drops due fields, so a later upgrade backfills those again using the configured hours and then-current priority.
''';p.write_text(s)
Path('docs/decisions/0010-fixed-response-deadlines.md').write_text('''# 10. Fixed response deadlines

Status: Accepted

Tickets need stable response promises and a safe production rollout. Store an additive optional `due` timestamp in the existing version 1 ticket record. Compute it once from creation time and priority with configurable response hours; never recompute a stored value. Backfill and save missing deadlines before startup completes, even while presentation remains disabled. No user action or notification is implied by this migration.

`DUE_TIMES=on` exposes deadlines and enables overdue filtering of active tickets with due strictly before the current clock. Leaving it off preserves the existing API and CLI presentation. Version 1 permits the 1.4.0 reader to ignore the extra field, so rollback can start and show every ticket. An old writer can discard deadlines; operators retain a backup if later restoring those promises is required.
''')
p=Path('docs/decisions/README.md');s=p.read_text();s+='| 10 | [Fixed response deadlines](0010-fixed-response-deadlines.md) | Accepted |\n';p.write_text(s)
PY
